sources.headline: India Cockroach Leaders Remain in Custody as Release Delayed
CJP alleges delay in release of leaders, 4 sureties rejected

brief_bullets: India’s Cockroach Janta Party raised concerns over what it described as “systematic delays and procedural obstruction” by Delhi Police and other authorities in securing the release of two of its leaders who have now spent five days in custody.

New Delhi: The bail hearing of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka was "delayed" on Sunday as the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) did not arrive at the scheduled time, activist Ratna Singh said and alleged that four sureties had been rejected on "vague" grounds.
Das and Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody on October 14 after they entered Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site, by scaling its locked gates.
The CJP leaders maintained that they had unfurled the national flag and raised slogans.
why_it_matters_bullets: Shifts federal policy priorities and legislative momentum ahead of upcoming electoral and administrative deadlines.

stories.primary_headline: Delhi: Class 12 student stabbed to death outside school, five apprehended

primary_source.headline: Delhi: Class 12 student stabbed to death outside school, five apprehended
primary_source.content: New Delhi: A 17-year-old Class 12 student was allegedly stabbed to death outside a government school in southwest Delhi's Mohan Garden area following an altercation between two students over the prescribed school shoes, police said on Sunday.Five accused, including three minors and two adults, have been apprehended in connection with the murder, three of whom are students of the same school, they said.The incident took place on October 14 when a PCR call regarding a stabbing incident near a government school in Mohan Garden was received at 6.10 pm at the local police station. The victim, a resident of Mohan Garden, had sustained stab injuries and was taken to Tarak Hospital, where he succumbed during treatment, the police said.Class 11 student fatally stabbed in south Delhi; two heldAccording to an eyewitness, a Class 12 student of the same school, the dispute began after another student complained to a teacher that he was not wearing the prescribed school-pattern shoes. This led to a heated argument between the two, during which the latter allegedly threatened him.After school hours, when the student left the premises with his friends, including the victim, the other student allegedly instigated the remaining accused, following which the group assaulted them. During the attack, one of the assailants allegedly stabbed the victim, causing fatal injuries, the police said.The knife allegedly used in the crime was recovered near the school gate.The victim's father is an ex-serviceman and is currently employed as a gunman in Gurugram, police said.

stories.primary_headline: They came to see Kolkata's famous pandals, but never returned home

primary_source.headline: They came to see Kolkata's famous pandals, but never returned home
primary_source.content: Kolkata: Pranjal Sarkar had no visible injuries anywhere else on his body. The only mark was that of a shoe on the left side of his face, a grim imprint of the brutal force of the footstep of an unknown person who may have unwittingly crushed the 13-year-old to death when the crowd surged at the Durga Puja pandal in Chorbagan in north-central Kolkata.Pranjal watched videos of the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samiti’s pandal on social media. The 13-year-old might not have fully grasped the “Beyond Sound” theme conceived and brought to life by artist Susanta Shibani Paul, but the sight of Goddess Durga and her four children, Kartik, Ganesh, Lakshmi and Saraswati, seated on a crescent moon amid dim, celestial lighting, caught his imagination. He insisted that the pandal be a must-see when his parents, Anukul Sarkar and Priyanka Sarkar, brought him from Agarpara in the North 24 Parganas district to Kolkata on the second day of the autumn festival.Little did Pranjal or his parents know that a danger lurked beneath the pandal’s surreal ambience, one that would turn the family’s Durga Puja outing into an unimaginable tragedy.The boy was one of the 19 people killed in the stampede at the pandal on Saturday. His parents survived, though. “He would have left for a tour to Shillong today with my sister and brother-in-law. Instead, I had to see the lifeless body of my nephew,” Pranjal’s maternal uncle said in front of the mortuary of Kolkata Medical College and Hospital on Sunday. “My brother-in-law could save seven or eight other children, but not his own son.”Even as the autumn festival unfolded across West Bengal, the stampede cast a pall of gloom over the families of the deceased and their neighbourhoods, from Kolkata and the Hooghly, Purba Bardhaman, North 24 Parganas and Nadia districts of West Bengal to Muzaffarpur in Bihar, turning what should have been a time of celebration into one of mourning.Kolkata stampede: Families mourn loss of loved ones as evening of festivity turned into heartacheSriparna Poddar, a 27-year-old nurse at a hospital in Kolkata, was often the first person her neighbours in Baidyabati, Hooghly, approached for healthcare advice. But on Sunday, she lay dead among the other victims of the stampede, while her family and neighbours waited to take home her mortal remains.Sandeep Bej, another 13-year-old boy, wanted to stay in his village in Madhabdihi in Purba Bardhaman for the Durga Puja celebrations but, at the last moment, went to Kolkata with his mother, Tagar Bej, 37, to see some of the city's pandals. However, the mother-son duo died in the stampede. So did Tagar’s sister, Piyali. Sandeep’s sister, Agamani Bej, was injured. “They were expected to return to their village on Sunday. But now only their mortal remains will return.”Ram Biswas came from Chakdaha in Nadia with his wife, Arati Sarkar Biswas, for pandal-hopping in Kolkata. He survived the stampede at Chorbagan but could not save his wife. Recalling the horror, Ram said that the crowd surged into the pandal after the ropes restricting entry were removed when it started raining. “It was dark inside, and people rushing in knocked others to the ground. Arati and I fell. I somehow got up and tried to pull her to her feet, but I couldn’t. My wife died before my eyes. I could do nothing,” Ram said on Sunday.For Abhishek Srivastava and his 13-year-old son, Ayansh, the trip to Kolkata was meant to be their first experience of the city’s famed Durga Puja celebrations. The two travelled from Muzaffarpur in Bihar to visit relatives in Agarpara, West Bengal, and went pandal-hopping with family members on Saturday. But both died in the stampede.Tania Biswas and Barnali Haldar, both 17, had planned their Maha Saptami outing well in advance. The Class XI students from Gouranga Nagar in New Town were close friends who had decided to wear sarees for the occasion. They set out with five other friends to visit the city’s Durga Puja pandals, but the outing ended in tragedy in Chorbagan, where both died in the stampede.Barnali’s father, Binod Haldar, who ekes out a living by pulling a rickshaw around New Town, learnt of his daughter’s death while he was still working. Her friends called him, and he rushed to the hospital, only to find that his elder child had already died. He spent the night outside the hospital mortuary. “My world has ended,” he said in a trembling voice, with tears rolling down his cheeks. “There will never be a Durga Puja in our lives again.”

Pranjal watched videos of the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samiti’s pandal on social media. The 13-year-old might not have fully grasped the “Beyond Sound” theme conceived and brought to life by artist Susanta Shibani Paul, but the sight of Goddess Durga and her four children, Kartik, Ganesh, Lakshmi and Saraswati, seated on a crescent moon amid dim, celestial lighting, caught his imagination. Triggers heightened municipal security deployments and intensifies scrutiny over public safety and emergency protocols.

stories.primary_headline: ‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva laid to rest amid tears, tributes

primary_source.headline: ‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva laid to rest amid tears, tributes
primary_source.content: Ranipet (Tamil Nadu): Veteran Tamil music composer and singer Deva, popularly known as 'Thenisai Thendral', was laid to rest with full state honours at his family farmland in Sakkaramallur near Arcot, Ranipet district, on Sunday.He was 75.Deva died of a heart attack in Chennai on the morning of October 17.His mortal remains were taken from his Chennai residence to the farmland, where the final rites were performed.Thousands of people gathered at the site to pay their last respects to the celebrated music director.Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay had visited Deva's residence in Chennai to pay his respects and announced that the funeral would be held with state honours in recognition of the composer's contribution to the music industry.Revenue and police officials oversaw arrangements for the ceremony at Sakkaramallur.‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva (1950-2026): The maestro who took gaana to the masses Relatives and villagers recalled Deva's enduring connection to his roots, saying he regularly visited his native village during festivals such as Pongal and contributed to local initiatives, including funding the construction of a Sri Ranganathar temple.Born Devanesan Chokkalingam, Deva had a career spanning nearly four decades and composed music for more than 400 films in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam.Before turning to films, Deva was an employee of the Tamil Nadu government’s Public Works Department (PWD).He made his entry as a composer in 1986 with 'Mattukkara Mannaru', which did not fare well in theatres, though its songs found a loyal audience over time.'Manasukketha Maharasa' (1989), starring Ramarajan and Seetha, was the film that first drew attention to his work. His real breakthrough, however, came in 1990 with the Prashanth-starrer 'Vaigasi Poranthachu', which won him widespread acclaim.Deva rose to prominence in the late 1980s and 1990s with his high-energy, folk-rooted tunes, and is widely credited with bringing the ‘gaana’ genre into mainstream Tamil cinema.Few composers in Tamil cinema are as closely identified with one genre as Deva is with 'gaana', the urban folk music born in the working-class neighbourhoods of North Chennai.He worked with nearly every leading star of his time, among them Vijayakanth, Sarathkumar, Vijay and Ajith, and delivered some of the biggest hits of their careers.Among his chartbusters were the Rajinikanth films ‘Annamalai’, ‘Baashha’ and ‘Arunachalam’, and the Kamal Haasan outings ‘Avvai Shanmugi’, ‘Pammal K Sambandam’ and ‘Panchathanthiram’.His death drew tributes from political leaders, members of the film fraternity and fans across Tamil Nadu.

primary_source.headline: Businessman shot at near Baramati Airport in Pune district
primary_source.content: Mumbai: In a shocking incident, a businessman, Rana Suryawanshi, was shot at near the Baramati Airport in the Pune district on Sunday.The Pune Rural Police has registered a case and investigations are in progress. “The news of gunfire targeting Rana Suryavanshi, the owner of Rana Shipping Company, in the vicinity of Baramati Airport is extremely shocking. Fortunately, he has survived and is currently receiving treatment,” Baramati MP Supriya Sule said. Shiv Sena (UBT) leader's murder: Police nab shooter, accomplice from Raigad“This news highlights the dire state of law and order in the state. Criminals are brazenly carrying out shootings and escaping, while the Home Department's machinery is unable to act. The public lives in fear, and it seems like criminals have been given free rein,” she said. “The Home Department should immediately take note of this incident, arrest the attackers, and implement concrete measures for the safety of citizens,” she added.

stories.primary_headline: No lift, no ramp: Kolar taluk office leaves elderly struggling

primary_source.headline: No lift, no ramp: Kolar taluk office leaves elderly struggling
primary_source.content: Kolar: The common man often has to struggle to get work done at government offices, with delays, demands for money, interference by middlemen and official apathy making the process difficult. Many people are even apprehensive about visiting these offices, as getting routine public services done without hassle remains a challenge.Adding to their woes, a long-pending problem at the Taluk Office building in Kolar continues to inconvenience the elderly and persons with disabilities. With no lift or ramp to access the first floor, they are forced to climb the stairs to get their work done.Distressing gaps in senior healthcareThe office of the sub-registrar, located on the first floor, is among the key offices in the building. Hundreds of people visit it every day for property, site and marriage registrations. A significant number of them are elderly or persons with disabilities, for whom climbing the stairs is a daunting task.In some cases, people who cannot walk have to be carried up the stairs, turning what should be a routine visit into an ordeal. Some struggle up the steps with the help of walking sticks, while others depend on family members or companions to climb up and down.Although a wheelchair is available at the entrance to the office, there is no ramp to take users to the first floor. A ramp has been provided only at the building's entrance.Four in 10 Bengalureans dread stepping into a lift: Survey     A branch of the sub-registrar's office has been opened on the ground floor to assist those unable to climb the stairs. However, visitors complain that staff are sometimes unavailable there. Several organisations have, therefore, urged the authorities to shift the entire sub-registrar's office to the ground floor. The office was earlier located near Prabhat Theatre in the City.The problem is not new. For several years, representatives of various organisations and senior citizens have been demanding the installation of a lift. Several tahsildars, deputy commissioners and MLAs have come but the lift remains a promise.Buildings housing major government offices are expected to be accessible to senior citizens and persons with disabilities. However, the lack of basic facilities at taluk office building has left many struggling to access public services.A lift should have been installed when the building was constructed, but the requirement appears to have been overlooked.Karnataka: Citizens suffer as new taluks lack admin buildingsLakshminarayanaswamy, a resident of Urigili in Kolar, said several government offices at taluk office building are located on the first floor. How are senior citizens and persons with disabilities expected to reach them? People are being carried up the stairs even for something as simple as obtaining a signature or completing other formalities. The taluk and district administrations should address the issue immediately, he urged.Prem Sagar Gowda, a resident of Markandapura in Kolar said the sub-registrar's office at the taluk office building is on the first floor. We can manage the stairs but shouldn't the authorities consider the difficulties faced by the elderly and persons with disabilities? A lift should be installed immediately. Alternatively, the entire sub-registrar's office should be shifted to the ground floor.Srinivas, Kolar TahsildarMLA Kottur Manjunath has taken the initiative to install a lift with the help of corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds. He is aware of the problem and the lift is expected to be ready within a few months easing the difficulties faced by visitors.
